decision: Initialize the Sourcera application in this repository after the delivery control plane passes.
assumption: No separate application repository or deployable branch currently exists.
validationTrigger: A verified application repository or explicit repository-boundary decision appears.

decision: Use one active implementation lane with WIP limit 1.
assumption: Current human capacity supports one reviewed change at a time.
validationTrigger: Two completed reviewed batches establish throughput or another active delivery owner joins.

decision: Blake Rowley is the interim accountable owner and named release or checkpoint approver. Required CI and a separate Codex reviewer provide independent change review first. No second human reviewer is fabricated.
assumption: The Linear workspace contains Blake Rowley and the Linear app; Blake Rowley is the only human member.
validationTrigger: A second active human member joins; require a distinct human reviewer, separate issue owner and reviewer, then recalibrate lanes, WIP, and capacity before qualifying more work.

decision: Live release scanners override copied or stale Master Spec header counts.
assumption: Volatile counts can change without a header rewrite.
validationTrigger: A deterministic generated-header mechanism replaces authored counts.

decision: Release assignments use source semantics, dependency closure, and explicit R0 critical-path overrides.
assumption: The current six-release model is the smallest reversible plan consistent with the stated customer journeys.
validationTrigger: A source change, customer pilot, or delivery-owner review disproves an assignment.

decision: Each runtime gate follows the named product behavior selected by source-section and assertion matching plus reviewed overrides.
assumption: The current feature inventory is the canonical behavior index for runtime proof routing.
validationTrigger: The feature inventory or a runtime assertion changes, or deployed evidence identifies a different owning behavior.

decision: Implement Master Spec §1.1 as three independently deployable Next.js applications for Buyer, Seller, and Marketplace with shared packages limited to cross-domain contracts.
assumption: No separate console repositories or conflicting deployment boundary exist.
validationTrigger: A verified external console repository or deployment constraint requires a different boundary.

decision: F-005 Convex persistence foundation precedes F-002 dual-console data isolation.
assumption: The unified Convex database named in §1.5 is the required persistence boundary for §1.3 isolation.
validationTrigger: A verified alternative persistence boundary or Master Spec change replaces Convex for F-002.

decision: F-006 WorkOS authentication follows the F-001 shell and F-005 Convex foundations, then precedes F-002 dual-console data isolation.
assumption: The §1.3 firewall requires a verified WorkOS identity and active Organization context before it can enforce tenant or console scope.
validationTrigger: A verified non-WorkOS identity boundary or Master Spec change replaces the §1.1 and §6.1 authentication contract.

decision: Forecast one WIP-1 batch at a time from completed reviewed batches and separate active work from external wait.
assumption: The first two R0 foundation batches provide a low-confidence active-work baseline but cannot support a calendar delivery date.
validationTrigger: Recalculate after every completed reviewed batch, any result outside the forecast band, or any capacity change.

decision: Urgent means non-terminal R0 work in the active codex-ready queue or a direct blocker of that queue; all other work uses release and dependency order without Urgent priority.
assumption: Priority must encode current execution order, while release placement and dependencies retain strategic importance without inflation.
validationTrigger: Re-evaluate Urgent whenever the active release, ready queue, or direct blocker set changes.

decision: Keep F-023 at its audited R1 baseline and add no R0 dependency edge.
assumption: The one-buyer R0 journey does not currently reach the explicit Solo Mode surface.
validationTrigger: Confirm whether the R0 pilot runs Solo Mode or the team engine with one buyer; add a source-pinned edge only if Solo Mode is required.

decision: Keep the audited invitation and delivery baselines and add no F-009 scheduling edge.
assumption: R0 includes seller invitation and magic-link arrival but the graph does not reach transactional email delivery.
validationTrigger: Prove the invitation transport in the Master Spec and runtime; add F-009 only if that transport owns delivery.

decision: Keep the audited identity baselines and do not split or add identity dependencies without source proof.
assumption: R0 authentication reaches WorkOS integration, while user, session, and org-provisioning contracts remain in later capabilities and F-161 bundles basic and enterprise identity.
validationTrigger: Pin the minimum R0 identity and session contract or split enterprise-only behavior before changing dependencies.

decision: Keep actor-role features at their audited baselines and add only acceptance-path-proved role edges.
assumption: RBAC enforcement is in closure, but the initial org owner, workspace owner, and bid owner roles are not.
validationTrigger: Trace the authorized actors for workspace creation, phase advancement, scoring, and seller submission; add only the roles required by those acceptance paths.

decision: Include phase locking, the advancement API, idempotency, audit, and gate validation in R0 through the source-pinned Phase 1 dependency chain.
assumption: F-211 now reaches F-210 and F-235 through F-238, while rendered surface mappings remain separately unproved.

decision: Keep buyer console shell features at their audited baselines and add no broad shell dependency.
assumption: The buyer-operated R0 journey has no dependency on the Buyer Console shell or layout contract.
validationTrigger: Trace the first buyer route and attach the smallest source-owned shell dependency.

decision: Keep rubric and score-history features at their audited baselines until R0 scoring proof requires them.
assumption: The scoring engine and lifecycle are in closure, but the grading rubric and per-change score history are not.
validationTrigger: Prove whether R0 acceptance requires rubric selection and score-change audit history; add the exact source-owned edges.

decision: Use F-226 as the narrow R0 Selection Report owner, keep F-592 at R2, and reject F-171 as the Selection Record export owner.

validationTrigger: Validate the R0 Selection Report format in the customer journey; add a narrower §40.1 owner only if F-226 does not fully supply the required portable record.

decision: Keep compressed surface mappings and conformance gates at their audited baselines until rendered R0 routes prove them.
assumption: R0 uses buyer and seller pipelines, but their compressed surface mappings and conformance gates remain outside closure.
validationTrigger: Run the R0 buyer and seller routes against the binding step-to-phase tables and add only the gates that prove rendered behavior.

decision: Keep the access-policy CI validator at its audited baseline until it is proved as a slice-one prerequisite.
assumption: Runtime access enforcement is in closure, but the feature-access acceptance-criteria validator is not.
validationTrigger: Confirm whether this validator is a prerequisite CI control for slice one; attach it to the access policy if required.

decision: Keep F-818 at its audited baseline until its exact Seller Maya behavior owner is proved.
assumption: The full AI seller onboarding journey is in R0, but the Seller Maya engine-mutation conformance gate remains later.
validationTrigger: Map F-818 to the exact R0 Seller Maya behavior owner or document why the gate is not required for the pilot.

decision: Keep hero instrumentation at its audited baseline and do not reverse its dependency without cycle-safe proof.

validationTrigger: Resolve dependency direction without creating a cycle, then prove Stage 3 latency and abandonment events in the R0 pilot.

decision: Keep F-179 and F-566 at their audited R5 baselines until the recovery contract is split or explicitly accepted.
assumption: Setup checklist recovery is an R2 operation but its dependency bundles enterprise organization settings, forcing both to R5.
validationTrigger: Split the narrow onboarding-settings recovery contract or accept R5 placement with an explicit product decision.

decision: Keep F-161 and F-609 at their audited R5 baselines until staff and customer identity are split or explicitly accepted.

decision: Retire F-608 through F-611 and preserve every capability in its dedicated §42 and §50 successor; never implement is_staff, unsafe one-click impersonation/export, a parallel admin_audit_log, or forever retention.
assumption: Master Spec §43.0–§43.5 explicitly retires all four v6 contracts and provides a complete successor map.
validationTrigger: If the Master Spec restores a retired contract, reconcile it against §50 without duplicating or weakening the active Ops controls.

decision: Keep F-104 at R4 and do not guess a different owner.
assumption: Buyer Console Entity Set contains the R0 Workspace, Use Case, Requirement, Response, Score, and firewall family, but is not reached by approved R0 roots.
validationTrigger: Decide whether F-104 is executable aggregation or catalog-only; if executable, add a source-proved R0 dependency edge, otherwise correct its disposition.

decision: Include F-213 in R0 as mandatory Phase 3 between F-212 and F-214.
assumption: Master Spec §10 defines a sequential no-skip evaluation pipeline, and the source-pinned F-212 to F-213 to F-214 dependency chain now makes that journey executable.
validationTrigger: Re-evaluate only if the Master Spec changes the no-skip contract or a reviewed reduced-pipeline contract replaces it without losing the R0 customer outcome.

decision: Keep F-505 at R5 and do not imply R0 runtime readiness.
assumption: Account lockout belongs to R5 enterprise and security at baseline, but the R0 brief also requires baseline security and the current R0 graph does not reach it.
validationTrigger: Confirm whether R0 authentication acceptance requires F-505 and add an auth-to-lockout edge if proved.

decision: Keep F-AE-006 at R5 because RTL is its latest binding behavior.
assumption: F-AE-006 combines print, reduced motion, RTL, and presence across R1, R2, and R5 capabilities.
validationTrigger: Split the source row into independently owned behaviors or record an approved earliest-consumer rule.

decision: Keep F-AE-029 at R4 pending seller-surface proof.
assumption: Seller bid-lifecycle phase mapping is R4 by its section location but directly binds the seller journey to the buyer R0 pipeline; no approved root reaches it.
validationTrigger: Prove whether the R0 seller surface reads this mapping and add the corresponding source-pinned closure edge if required.

decision: Keep F-634 at its audited baseline and do not invent an implementation release.
assumption: Known Limitations and Phase 2 Roadmap is planning prose marked executable and cannot name an owning release capability.
validationTrigger: Change its disposition or decompose each actual deferred behavior into executable source rows.

decision: Keep F-785 at R3 until its aggregate ownership is decomposed.
assumption: The aggregate state-machine compendium spans R1 through R4 behaviors but is a single R3 executable row.
validationTrigger: Confirm whether it is catalog-only or split it by owning state-machine capability.

decision: Keep F-886 at R3 to avoid silent scope loss.
assumption: Product-wide voice and tone guidance has no dependency or release-specific owner; current R3 placement is a keyword artifact.
validationTrigger: Bind it to the earliest executable surface family or mark it as a non-executable design constraint.

decision: Keep unsplit F-567 at R5.
assumption: F-567 combines profile and notification settings with MFA, API tokens, session control, GDPR export, and deletion, and depends on R5 WorkOS Authentication Architecture.
validationTrigger: Decompose F-567 into profile/notification settings and security/privacy/API/session children; then place each child at its earliest complete owner.

decision: Keep unsplit F-738 at R4.
assumption: F-738 mixes Marketplace trust with AI-operation spend and contest analysis and depends on ContestRecord F-128, which remains final R4.
validationTrigger: Split listing/signup/payout trust panels from AI-spend and contest panels, or approve F-128 earlier with its complete contest workflow.

decision: Compare live Linear milestone fingerprints by stable id, name, full description fingerprint, project ID, and project name, while preserving any existing planning dates and update metadata in the snapshot.
assumption: Linear exposes the full milestone description but not milestone updatedAt or targetDate through the current capture path, so exact description and project topology are the reversible live drift boundary.
validationTrigger: Add LINEAR_API_KEY or gain connector parity for both date fields, verify capture parity, then re-enable milestone updatedAt and targetDate comparison.

decision: Keep production staging and promotion fail-closed until the repo pins the exact Convex production target, every Vercel application has a healthy READY production predecessor, and a protected pre-mutation canary proves the live known-good Convex SHA from a clean detached checkout.
assumption: Live provider evidence shows no selected Convex deployment, no Marketplace production target, and failed Buyer and Seller production targets; no live rollback anchor currently exists.
validationTrigger: Re-evaluate only after reviewed provider provisioning or a separately approved bootstrap supplies the exact target, healthy predecessors, stable domains, and a live runtime whose protected canary identity matches the recorded known-good SHA; historical receipts remain context, never authority.

decision: Keep GitHub Actions as the protected production-mutation boundary and require real R0 customer and operational proof against staged Vercel deployments plus an isolated candidate Convex deployment through a durable pause-and-resume coordinator before final promotion; until that coordinator and collectors exist, fail closed and restore the proved production Convex release.
assumption: The current applications are deployment shells, no protected release-control project or isolated candidate Convex target is pinned, and an invited-human pilot cannot be truthfully completed inside the one-shot release job.
validationTrigger: Implement and review the isolated candidate target, authenticated proof collectors, protected release-control project, durable Vercel Workflow hooks, expiry compensation, single-use promotion lease, and GitHub finalizer; then run a real invited-human staging pilot and rollback drill before enabling promotion.

decision: Create the first Vercel production predecessor set only through a separate protected baseline workflow: pin all three domains and the exact Convex target, stage and prove all three candidates before traffic, persist one immutable stage receipt, then activate Marketplace, Buyer, and Seller in order. A partial first activation is recovery_required and may resume only from the same receipt; it never claims rollback.
assumption: Vercel activates projects independently and there is no earlier healthy deployment to restore during the first baseline. Live provider state currently has no Marketplace production domain and no healthy production target for any application.
validationTrigger: Provision and review every missing domain and target pin, configure the protected GitHub environment and Vercel credential, pass all release gates, then run a no-traffic staging proof and reviewed baseline activation. Reconsider strict rollback only after every project has a separate healthy maintenance predecessor.

decision: Keep all ordinary and bootstrap provider mutation disabled while DEC-PROD-002 is blocked. Bootstrap may create only non-promotable, attempt-bound authority after an exhaustive GitHub anchor inventory proves true first genesis or exact expired-anchor recovery; no process or job may receive both Vercel and Convex write credentials.
assumption: A one-shot controller cannot safely hold both provider credential classes or prove single-use recovery authority before the durable coordinator, phase receipts, compensation jobs, and finalizer exist.
validationTrigger: Implement and review receipt-bound Vercel stage, isolated proof, Convex mutation, Vercel promotion, provider-specific compensation, attempt-specific GitHub evidence, and a single-use finalizer; then prove cancellation and rollback drills before enabling any mutation job.

decision: Treat GitHub Actions artifact inventory as retained evidence only. It may support a non-promotable blocked anchor, but it never proves permanent first-ever or single-use authority after artifact expiry, deletion, workflow deletion, or workflow rename.
assumption: GitHub Actions artifacts are retention-bound and can be deleted, so absence from the live artifact API cannot prove that no historical production authority ever existed.
validationTrigger: Before any bootstrap authority can authorize provider mutation, persist and validate a non-expiring protected genesis sentinel plus a single-use finalizer whose history survives workflow and artifact retention changes.

decision: Preserve the application-header outcome as F-910, replace the canceled ticket literals with a typed per-origin and per-response policy, and keep it not codex-ready.
assumption: The Master Spec owns rich-content and Ops CSP boundaries but does not yet own the complete customer-surface header and provider matrix.
validationTrigger: Ratify the matrix in the Master Spec, or revalidate when an origin, provider, or legitimate report-only violation changes an allowance.

decision: Preserve the browser cross-origin outcome as F-911 with same-origin default, exact approved origins, credentials off unless required, bounded preflight caching, and fail-closed unknown origins.
assumption: The Master Spec owns isolation and API boundaries but is silent on the exact CORS matrix; the defaults are reversible and lower-authority.
validationTrigger: Ratify the CORS matrix, approve a new browser client, or reconcile a legitimate denied preflight before codex-ready.

decision: Normalize custom branding to one Organization-scoped Buyer Enterprise outcome and exclude vanity hosting, certificates, tenant routing, and export branding.
assumption: Current authority names entitlement, Organization logo, contrast, logo, favicon, and accent behavior but not the complete entity, surface, downgrade, or waiver matrix.
validationTrigger: The Master Spec authors that matrix or Product and Design approve a different surface set; then reconcile migrations, fixtures, and proof.

decision: Preserve deterministic reference-data bootstrap as F-913 while prohibiting seeded users, seeded administrators, customer fixtures, and automatic pricing publication.
assumption: Current authority owns template materialization, pricing-version immutability, and first-user admin provisioning but not the bootstrap manifest schema or promotion command.
validationTrigger: The Master Spec authors the bootstrap contract or the named business owners approve the schema, payloads, environments, and approvers.

decision: Create one R2 shared Card surface contract from the contiguous UX token and state authority; earlier journey cards remain valid and cannot depend on this later consolidation.
assumption: UX Design has no standalone Card heading, so the exact §2.3 through §2.5 slice plus named Master consumers is the narrow reversible source boundary.
validationTrigger: A higher-authority Card contract is authored or an active canonical owner is found; merge into that owner and retire F-914 if complete.

decision: Create one R1 buyer vendor-response comparison outcome from Master Spec §3.3.3 and treat the conflicting UX §4.2.8 summary pointer as non-authoritative.
assumption: The Master Spec explicitly owns the comparison behavior; the UX heading named by summary prose resolves to Intelligence Dashboard and cannot override it.
validationTrigger: A live active issue is found to own the complete comparison outcome or the Master Spec changes the behavior; merge without feature loss.

decision: Split the mandatory Buyer Business Starter trial activation into R0 as F-916 and narrow F-533 to the later day-11 through day-15 lifecycle; production Buyer Org creation stays disabled until F-916 can atomically commit its trial, plan, wallet, allowance, reference, Stripe-Customer, and audit overlay. Treat the explicit §34.9.1 $50 figure as the total 14-day trial wallet budget until §34 authors a different calculation.
assumption: Master Spec §34.9.1 makes trial activation part of every new Buyer-console Org signup, while the prior aggregate F-533 R2 assignment created an invalid Buyer Free fallback. Its wallet row states both a $50 included budget and that the monthly cap is prorated, but supplies no divisor, rounding, timezone, or billing-period formula; the explicit dollar figure is the least inventive reversible default.
validationTrigger: If §34 changes the Buyer signup plan, authors a trial-budget proration formula, or an existing canonical feature is proved to own this activation transaction, reconcile F-916 without dropping its R0 behavior, failure, recovery, rollout, or proof contracts and migrate only unconsumed trial budget under an audited plan.

decision: Keep canceled PLA-162 unresolved and preserve its vanity-host provenance; treat F-166 / PLA-338 as related DNS verification and auto-join governance, not a behavioral successor.
assumption: Master Spec §6.4 and §48.5.6 govern email-domain verification and auto-join, while UX §8.8 describes a distinct vanity-host capability; silence does not authorize deletion.
validationTrigger: Resolve only when the Master Spec or §34 explicitly accepts, changes, or retires customer vanity application hosting.

decision: Retire the generic Alert ticket and preserve transient notification, connectivity, amendment warning, and recoverable error behavior in their four named vertical owners.
assumption: Current authority deliberately separates these behaviors; a generic Alert would create an ungoverned duplicate path.
validationTrigger: Archive only after every preserved variant, failure, recovery, accessibility, telemetry, and proof contract is linked and verified.

decision: Retire the generic InsightCard mutation and preserve disagreement, seller suggestion, and read-only predictive insight behavior in their capability-specific owners.
assumption: Current authority assigns different action semantics and forbids persisted generic accept or dismiss for predictive suggestions.
validationTrigger: Archive only after all named owners are linked and tests prove predictive suggestions remain read-only.

decision: Split first Stripe Customer genesis into R0 as F-917 and implement the Master Spec's externally atomic Organization-creation promise through an idempotent provider action, an atomic Convex binding mutation, and compensating Customer closure when the binding cannot commit; no public route reports success until both provider and database state agree.
assumption: Convex mutations cannot perform Stripe network calls inside a database transaction, so literal single-transaction execution is unavailable while the required user-visible all-or-nothing outcome remains achievable and reversible.
validationTrigger: If Convex adds transactional external calls or the Master Spec authors a different orchestration contract, replace this mapping while preserving one active Customer, complete metadata, idempotency, rollback, audit, and no-partial-success guarantees.

decision: A verified payment method alone never authorizes a paid trial conversion. Day-15 paid conversion requires an explicit stored chosen Buyer plan; otherwise the no-confirmed-conversion path returns the Organization to Buyer Free without charging the stored method.
assumption: Master Spec §34.9.1 says conversion is to the chosen plan tier but does not define a default paid tier or authorize a charge when no plan was chosen. The no-charge fallback is the safest reversible commercial default.
validationTrigger: If §34 authors a default paid plan and explicit consent contract, replace this fallback prospectively; never retroactively charge a completed or downgraded trial.

decision: Preserve Marketplace Review and Marketplace Integration Hook in F-628's 21-entity firewall inventory, but keep D1, D2, and D3 unready until each has a canonical §4.x entity, audience, route, lifecycle, privacy, and proof contract; do not delete, alias, or fabricate either feature.
assumption: Master Spec §1.3.2 and F-116 still name both features, while no current §4.x definition supplies enough evidence to build their positive or negative runtime matrices.
validationTrigger: The Master Spec authors complete contracts for both features or explicitly maps each to an existing canonical entity with verified no-loss migration; then refresh the affected issue bodies and checksums.

decision: Do not create F-483.A or F-918 as an R0 webhook product feature from the F-628 test draft alone. Keep D4 unready until an approved release owner provides the complete §31.11 subscription guard, uniform event registry, and required transport prerequisites.
assumption: Current authority places Notification Event Catalog in R1, Webhook Notification Subscriptions in R2, and Webhook Delivery System in R4; F-628 testing authority does not by itself authorize moving those product behaviors into R0.
validationTrigger: Product ratifies a complete R0 producer and all prerequisite release moves, or D4 is moved to the earliest release with a complete producer; then bind D4 to the exact live issue and rerun topology/inversion checks.

decision: F-916 owns only the §48.1.1 and §48.1.4 signup-stage UsageEvent/outbox pair required by Buyer activation. F-636 and F-637 retain the later full-funnel stages and their F-527 dependency, so they are not promoted into R0 through F-916.
assumption: The Buyer activation route must emit the registered signup events before success, but it does not implement Aha Moment, Ceiling Hit, Expansion, Enterprise Trigger, or later plan-change mechanics.
validationTrigger: If Product makes the full paid-path funnel an R0 deliverable, approve a source-backed split or move the complete F-527/F-636/F-637 dependency closure together; never add an inversion-only edge.

decision: Keep all five Stripe Customer metadata keys. Encode non-custom custom_sovereign_residency_label as the exact string sentinel not_applicable; custom residency uses the exact non-empty Organization label. Missing, null, empty, and string null values are invalid.

validationTrigger: If Stripe supports a typed nullable metadata value or §34 authors a different complete representation, migrate prospectively with dual-read proof and preserve historical metadata fidelity.

decision: Implement F-007 through one server-owned Stripe adapter pinned to stripe@22.3.2 and API/webhook version 2026-06-24.dahlia. Store encrypted provider references plus correlation hashes only in private orchestration rows; cancellation may be unscheduled before terminal cancellation, but a canceled Subscription is never resumed.
assumption: The pinned SDK/provider contract and current Master behavior are the narrowest reproducible boundary for Subscription, invoice, and meter reconciliation; provider calls remain outside Convex transactions.
validationTrigger: Any SDK, API, webhook-version, provider-event, or Master billing change invalidates readiness and requires request/response fixtures, state machines, recovery, and proof receipts to be regenerated.

decision: Resolve the Plan and Billing role conflict with the page-specific least-privilege R2 default: only an active same-Organization org_owner may read the page, download an authorized invoice, or launch the portal; plan and wallet mutations route to their owning features; Billing Admin remains unavailable until F-142 and the source conflict close.
assumption: Master §36.2 explicitly makes the page Org Owner only, while §5.2.1 grants broader billing capabilities without reconciling this surface; the narrower page rule avoids silently widening access.
validationTrigger: A Master amendment reconciles §36.2 with §5.2.1 and §34.12.4.A or F-142 ships a complete own-Org Billing Admin matrix; then update F-007.B tests and its ordered checksum before readiness.

decision: Treat F-007 operation, provider-event, meter-delivery, production-proof, and pilot-run rows as implementation-private records, not canonical customer entities or public APIs. Financial-control evidence uses the applicable §40.2 class; rejected pre-provider non-PII attempts purge after the issue-stated bounded window.
assumption: These rows coordinate retries and proof without introducing customer-facing domain concepts; exposing them would require entity, API, audit, lifecycle, privacy, and vocabulary authority that does not yet exist.
validationTrigger: If implementation needs a row to become public, customer-visible, or independently addressable, stop readiness and author its Master §4 schema/state machine, §40.2 rule, Appendix J values, API/audit contract, migration, and proof before use.

decision: Limit F-132 to the PricingTableVersion schema fragment, deterministic snapshot builder, immutable entity guard, and server-internal resolvers. F-499 owns the Public Pricing API; F-549 owns review, publication, supersession, notifications, reconciliation, and rollback. Admit the seven §34.14.5 status values for storage compatibility without owning their transitions.

validationTrigger: The Master reconciles §4.8.9 and §34.14.5 or changes the F-499/F-549 boundary; regenerate the F-132 checksum and revalidate fragment, status admission, consumer imports, migrations, and proof before codex-ready.

decision: Compile unaffected retention rows normally but return blocked for the duplicate Internal Comment key and the conflicting BillingSeatSnapshot and DowngradeExcessDataBucket keys. Array order, last-write-wins, or a local TTL may never resolve a source conflict.
assumption: Failing closed preserves data and feature scope while the Master contains contradictory destructive instructions; it is safer and reversible compared with choosing a shorter retention or deletion path.
validationTrigger: The Master names one canonical rule per conflicted key; regenerate the F-593 ordered checksum and pass duplicate, bidirectional coverage, residency, DSAR, financial, and destructive-consumer gates before enabling those resolutions.

decision: Remove the broad F-630 to F-687 block. The composed seller journey must build and prove before the release gate evaluates it; release-control status cannot be a prerequisite for the journey evidence that the same gate consumes.

decision: Keep BillingSeatSnapshot informational only: §34 forbids per-seat pricing, current unlimited plans store nullable plan_max_members_at_snapshot with no breach, and immutable financial source facts follow the §40.2 Org-life-plus-seven-year rule while compact daily, weekly, and monthly projections serve time-series reads.
assumption: The later pricing authority and retention registry must prevent a stale endpoint example, non-null compatibility field, or downsampling sentence from creating a charge, invented cap, or premature deletion.
validationTrigger: The Master reconciles §4.2.1, §4.8.11, §32.8.19, §34.7, and §40.2; regenerate the F-529 checksum and revalidate schema migration, API projection, retention, and no-per-seat proof.

decision: When entitlement authority is unavailable, return the bounded service-unavailable path and skip PostHog evaluation; do not claim the user is unentitled. An affirmative entitlement denial remains 403, and 403 wins only when the entitlement result itself is known.
assumption: The Master defines entitlement-denied and flag-disabled behavior but is silent on entitlement-provider outage; 503 is reversible and avoids converting an authority failure into a false permission judgment.
validationTrigger: The Master or the canonical entitlement contract authors an explicit outage result; update F-631 evaluation, UI recovery, tests, telemetry, and source checksum before readiness.

decision: F-005 is the sole owner of the deterministic convex/schema.ts assembler and explicit fragment registry. Feature issues own exact schema fragments only: F-132 pricingTableVersions, F-630 releaseGateRuns, and F-007 stripeBilling. Duplicate, missing, cyclic, wildcard-discovered, or unowned fragments fail code generation and CI.
assumption: The linked product repository can compose explicit typed table fragments before one defineSchema call; this is the smallest reversible ownership boundary that preserves every table without shared-file collisions.
validationTrigger: Convex code generation or the linked product repository proves a different supported assembly boundary; update F-005 and every fragment owner atomically, then rerun generated-model, path-collision, topology, and Linear readback gates.

decision: F-139 owns only the org_owner policy and live role-resolution contribution plus its role lifecycle and settings controls. F-160 owns the common API/UI enforcement adapter and entrypoint-coverage gate. F-139 depends on F-160 and cannot create a competing authorization path.
assumption: A role contribution can be added after the R0 enforcement foundation without widening the adapter or moving the R1 role into R0.
validationTrigger: The product repository exposes no bounded contribution seam or the Master moves org_owner into the R0 role matrix; revise both issues and their release topology together before readiness.

decision: F-630 owns the private server-only rollout-control registry and safe-off handlers used by F-007 and F-537. F-631 remains the closed catalog of 20 entitlement-aware customer flags. A private key can stop new work but cannot grant entitlement, alter pricing, or become customer-visible.
assumption: Master §46.3 can be implemented through a bounded private registry without expanding the exact §46.7 customer catalog.
validationTrigger: The Master authors a different generic control owner, expands the exact customer catalog, or makes a private key customer-visible; stop use, reclassify through source authoring, and update every dependency, handler, test, and proof receipt.

decision: F-007.E owns the bounded R2 journey target set r2_f007_billing_journey_v1, including all seven operators, values, windows, sample rules, approval fields, validator/generator behavior, and both customer and operational proof gates. The initial one-participant run is safety evidence only; release proof needs five valid starts across at least three consented Organizations.
assumption: The issue-stated thresholds are conservative reversible defaults because no approved live F-007 cohort baseline exists.
validationTrigger: An independently reviewed cohort supports a future version before a later release; it cannot rewrite or waive the approved target set governing its own runs, and any new version requires fresh scorecard, consent, dry run, and proof.

decision: Use exactly one primary Linear Layer label per issue because the live workspace enforces Layer as a single-choice group. Preserve secondary UI, backend, schema, integration, accessibility, and operations scope in the self-contained issue contract and exact paths instead of adding invalid same-group labels.
assumption: The current label-group constraint is workspace-native truth and one primary layer is sufficient for routing without changing issue scope.
validationTrigger: Linear label-group configuration changes or a multi-layer classification field is introduced; regenerate the exact label map and read back every affected issue without changing behavior ownership.

decision: F-922 is the sole canonical OpsActionRecord owner in R2; F-923 through F-930 are the sole full-outcome owners for Master §50.20 through §50.27 in R5. F-925 through F-930 remain unready until their compressed source sections are repaired, and F-608/F-610/F-611 cannot close until every successor and native relation exists.
assumption: The full §50.20 through §50.27 outcomes require mandatory API, webhook, enterprise identity, billing, retention, and Ops prerequisites whose current release closure reaches R5; earlier mergeable children may land sooner but cannot close the parent or erase later behavior.
validationTrigger: The Master authors a complete replacement contract, an independently reviewed decomposition proves an earlier release without inversion, or any named prerequisite changes; update inventory, dependencies, releases, Linear relations, checksums, and closure records together before readiness.

decision: Until the Master fixes the concrete §32 Use Case paths and undo correlation semantics, F-085.A uses DELETE /v1/workspaces/{workspace_id}/use-cases/{use_case_id} plus POST .../{use_case_id}/restore, binds the ten-second undo to the immutable delete AuditEvent correlation, and restores the exact Requirement and Scenario references removed by that correlation. No email, Inbox item, or webhook is emitted because the bound source defines none.
assumption: The REST-shaped paths, server-signed short-lived correlation, and exact no-loss restore are reversible before customer traffic and preserve the explicit Master behavior without a new persistent entity or invented notification.
validationTrigger: The Master authors a different route, undo-correlation model, Scenario-restore rule, or notification; update the issue, source bundle, registry, route clients, fixtures, and proof before readiness or rollout.

decision: Use actor_user_id as the sole canonical OpsActionRecord actor field; normalize DSAR and retention references to it and migrate any proved legacy acting_user_id storage without keeping an alias.
assumption: The entity table, index, event, and active-session validator already use actor_user_id, making it the smallest reversible canonical destination.
validationTrigger: A live schema inspection proves deployed acting_user_id storage; require the explicit conflict-safe migration and readback before changing any writer.

decision: Model linked_ops_session_id and co_approver_ops_session_id as nullable single OpsSession FKs, required for the acting and distinct co-approving signers when their action requires those sessions.
assumption: The current quorum model records one session-bearing action per signer and provides no evidence that one signer needs multiple linked sessions.
validationTrigger: Live authorization evidence proves multi-session cardinality or a different signer/session model; amend the source and migration before enforcement.

decision: Represent console_scope=both with explicit buyer and seller from/to tier pairs and record published then effective as one ordered local commit with a monotonic transition sequence.
assumption: Separate typed pairs prevent cross-console tier inference, while ordered evidence resolves equal effective timestamps without inventing a public dwell.
validationTrigger: The financial protocol requires a durable provider-to-local dwell or a different normalized payload; update schema, state timing, idempotency, and proofs together.

decision: Use PlanTierOverrideProposal plus a versioned provider-attempt record as the canonical retained financial evidence for manual plan overrides; do not create a parallel customer billing ledger.
assumption: This is the smallest model that preserves provider retries, compensation, reconciliation, and seven-year evidence without duplicating customer billing truth.
validationTrigger: Live billing schema proves an existing canonical record carries every required field and history; reuse it and retire the proposed attempt record before implementation.

decision: Register the existing plan-override role union and lifecycle names as closed capability, OpsActionRecord, error, webhook, and transactional-template catalogs without widening access or copying prices.
assumption: The prose role and lifecycle contract is intended but incomplete only at its catalog boundaries.
validationTrigger: Approved policy narrows a role, reclassifies an event, or changes a recipient/channel; update every matrix, catalog, test, and producer before enablement.

decision: Require two people for troubleshooting or migration exports and three people for DSAR or legal-hold exports, with exact role, session, residency, step-up, anti-collusion, and capability checks.
assumption: The stricter signer count for compliance exports is a reversible least-privilege default proportionate to their retained-data exposure.
validationTrigger: Approved privacy or legal policy mandates a stricter role or signer set; tighten the source matrix before enabling that export kind.

decision: Add cancelled, generation_retryable, and generation_failed request states plus immutable per-claim attempt rows, a five-attempt bounded schedule, leases, checkpoints, and terminal recovery rules.
assumption: Five attempts at immediate, one-minute, five-minute, thirty-minute, and two-hour intervals balance recoverability against sensitive-object exposure.
validationTrigger: Production-shaped load or provider constraints prove the schedule unsafe; revise state, retention, and worker proof before changing configuration.

decision: Use deterministic ZIP64 with canonical NDJSON files, a hashed manifest, deny-by-default per-profile field allowlists, region-local encrypted storage, and bounded archive limits for Workspace exports.
assumption: ZIP64 and NDJSON provide interoperable, streamable, versionable output while the deny-all fallback preserves privacy before each allowlist cell is approved.
validationTrigger: Performance, legal, or pilot evidence requires another format or limit; version the archive contract and preserve reader compatibility before rollout.

decision: Use download_consumed_at as the canonical timestamp, delete consumed and expired non-hold archives within twenty-four hours, and retain bounded request and attempt metadata for ninety days.
assumption: The entity already owns download_consumed_at, and prompt archive deletion minimizes exposure while preserving enough metadata for recovery and audit.
validationTrigger: An approved legal or customer contract requires a longer archive window; add a narrow encrypted and audited exception before changing purge behavior.

decision: Until the Master reconciles §1.4 with §46.5 item 3, interpret query_scoping_console_required as a global census of every live list endpoint that enforces each registered route's exact §1.4 scope: Organization-scoped routes require org_id and forbid console; Buyer and Seller console-scoped routes require org_id plus the exact buyer or seller console; managed Marketplace routes require console=marketplace plus their registered audience; public Marketplace routes require neither console nor an Organization session. Missing required scope, unexpected scope, and unregistered or misclassified routes fail closed. This interpretation is removable without a data migration after source reconciliation.
assumption: §1.4 is the route-specific behavior authority and §46.5 item 3 intended global coverage rather than an override of §1.4's explicit Organization-scoped and public-Marketplace omissions.
validationTrigger: A Master change or human source-owner ruling reconciles §1.4 and §46.5; before merge or readiness, update the registry, gate, tests, issue body, decision status, and ordered source checksum to the reconciled rule.

decision: To preserve §7.5 scope isolation without stale client leakage, bind every cursor, cache entry, subscription, export envelope, and reactive result to the verified Organization, console, workspace or audience, policy hash, and lineage that created it. When re-authentication changes verified scope or an authorized console switch changes active console, invalidate incompatible state before new data renders. Reconnect may resume only when verified scope, policy hash, and lineage are identical; otherwise start a fresh authorized query. This is a reversible fail-closed implementation default, not behavior authored by §7.5.
assumption: Master §7.5 requires subscriptions to remain isolated by org_id plus console plus workspace where applicable, but is silent on the exact client-state invalidation sequence after verified-scope change. Pre-render invalidation is the narrowest reversible default that prevents stale cross-scope data from remaining observable.
validationTrigger: The Master or a ratified identity/reactivity contract authors a different safe re-authentication, console-switch, cursor, cache, or subscription transition. Before readiness, update F-002/F-003 bodies, guards, fixtures, receipt schemas, tests, and this decision status together; retain fail-closed behavior until the replacement passes cross-scope negative proof.

decision: Treat the Master §9.1.2 Team Owner and Team Lead names as workflow labels over the canonical §5.5.1 Seller Console roles. F-198 and PLA-370 own the combined executable role-authority mapping; F-199 and archived PLA-371 retain no separate planning ownership.
assumption: One combined authority map is the smallest current model that preserves every Owner and Lead workflow while preventing a second role system.
validationTrigger: The Master authors a distinct Team Lead authority that cannot be represented by the canonical Seller Console roles; reactivate a separate source requirement and live issue only after source, permissions, tests, and migration review.
